title: Vision Transformers as a Framework for Imaging Fluorescence Correlation Spectroscopy
summary: Fluorescence correlation spectroscopy (FCS) is widely used for quantifying molecular dynamics in live cells. However, conventional FCS relies on the autocorrelation function (ACF), a lossy transformation that discards higher-order information, mathematically couples distinct biophysical parameters, and requires long measurements (~50,000 frames, or ~1 minute) that obscure short-lived transient events. To overcome this information bottleneck, we introduce ImFCSViT, a spatiotemporal Vision Transformer-based framework that bypasses the ACF representation entirely, operating directly on raw fluorescence image stacks. By introducing a dedicated normalization token to preserve global intensity statistics, our approach simultaneously extracts four biophysical parameters (diffusion coefficient D, particle density N, particle brightness B, and PSF structure factor {sigma}0) in a single forward pass. Requiring only 2.5 s of data, and potentially down to 1 s (a 1-2 order reduction in data requirement), our approach accurately recovers diffusion coefficients while utilizing its spatial field-of-view to reveal spatially heterogeneous, slow-diffusing sub-populations in lipid bilayers and live-cell plasma membranes that are invisible to classical FCS. By leveraging the data-driven representational learning capabilities of deep learning, we present a flexible, generalizable, and powerful tool for mapping complex, multi-parameter spatiotemporal dynamics in biological systems.

title: Integrating stool chemistry measurements with metagenomics in adults reveals distinct gut health profiles
summary: Stool chemistry metrics, including calprotectin, lactoferrin, and secretory IgA, are used to assess gut inflammation in clinical or research settings. However, these measures in isolation provide a limited view of gut physiology and lack microbial context. Shotgun metagenomics offers a comprehensive assessment of the gut microbiome's taxonomic composition and functional potential, yet its integration with stool chemistry metrics remains underexplored. We analyzed 877 adult stool samples with paired shotgun metagenomic sequencing and chemistry measurements to integrate the microbiome with 12 stool chemistry metrics. Calprotectin, lactoferrin, and secretory IgA were associated with shifts in microbiome composition (beta diversity), while deviations from typical levels of short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs), including butyrate, were associated with both changes in alpha diversity and microbiome composition. Network analysis revealed two distinct microbial neighborhoods: one associated with higher butyrate and lower calprotectin and lactoferrin and another associated with lower butyrate and higher calprotectin and lactoferrin. Machine learning models trained on taxonomic and functional data showed modest discrimination of stool chemistry states, performing best for SCFA deficiency and less well for host-derived inflammatory metrics. Together, these findings systematically characterize microbiome-stool chemistry relationships across a large paired dataset, providing a framework for interpreting stool chemistry metrics in the context of shotgun metagenomic profiles.

title: Sequence architecture of RNA reveals key molecular signatures driving RNA phase separation
summary: Biomolecular condensates are dynamic membraneless assemblies that organize various cellular processes through liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS). RNA is an active regulator of biomolecular condensates and influence their formation through sequence-encoded features. Despite its established role in condensate formation, no computational framework exists to identify underlying signatures to predict LLPS-associated RNAs. We develop an interpretable hybrid framework to distinguish reviewed, experimentally supported LLPS-associated RNAs from background RNAs. We uncover biologically meaningful sequence properties associated with condensate participation. Each RNA is represented by 167 handcrafted descriptors capturing composition, k-mer usage, sequence complexity, repeat organization and dinucleotide autocorrelation together with 640-dimensional contextual embeddings from RNA-FM. These representations are integrated through cross-validated stacking with neural-network meta-learner. The framework achieves an AUC-ROC of 0.935, AUC-PR of 0.944 and MCC of 0.782. Feature statistics, ablation analysis and SHAP interpretation reveal a distributed sequence architecture dominated by altered local k-mer usage with additional contributions from low-complexity burden, repeat-associated organization and long-range dinucleotide pattern. Biological case studies including MALAT1 and TMPO-AS1 further connect these patterns with experimentally characterized modes of multivalent RNA-protein assembly. Together, the results show how interpretable machine learning can move beyond prediction to identify sequence features that generate mechanistic hypotheses for RNA-mediated condensation.

title: Human CYP1A2 metabolism of organophosphorus pesticides and nerve agent surrogates
summary: CYP1A2 contributes 13-15% of hepatic CYP450 content and plays a critical role in the metabolism of approximately 10% of pharmaceutical drugs in the human body. CYP1A2 has been previously reported to bioactivate and detoxify both the thion (P=S) and oxon (P=O) forms of organophosphorus (OP) compounds. In this study, we determined the capacity of CYP1A2 to degrade OP compounds using LC-MS/MS, as well as the inhibition of its activity by OP compounds using the previously developed pFluor50 assay. CYP1A2 was selective in metabolizing thions over oxons, and several OP compounds inhibited its activity in a time- and dose-dependent manner. To further investigate the mechanism of CYP1A2-OP interactions, molecular docking studies were performed using a crystal structure of CYP1A2 (PDB ID: 2HI4). Linear correlation analysis between CYP1A2 inhibition at 10 M with 30 minute preincubation and the % OP compound remaining at 2 hours (R = -0.71, P<0.001) showed a moderate but significant correlation. Based on these findings, CYP1A2 was identified as a potential bioscavenger for OP compound metabolism, supporting the future integration of experimental and in silico data for developing artificial intelligence (AI) / machine learning (ML) models for prediction of CYP1A2-mediated metabolism of existing and emerging OP compounds, including those of toxicological and chemical warfare relevance.
